sm: The speaker, P. Andrew Sandlin, recalls advice a Staten Island pastor gave him about forty-seven years ago: make your brain sweat when you read. He says the mind grows stronger through hard work, like muscles, and describes struggling through difficult authors such as Cornelius Van Til, rereading paragraphs many times until the books became easy. He cites Mortimer Adler's point that great books are above everyone's head, which is why reading takes real work. He then notes an Atlantic article arguing that people read more words than ever, but only in snippets like memes and tweets, and are losing the ability to follow long arguments, which makes them easier to propagandize. He urges people to read long books and long essays, pointing to Romans and Hebrews, to aim for a whole book before year's end, to annotate and make their own index, and to reread difficult passages until they become clear.
